chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad and Abdillah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said to me: 'What is your opinion about it?' I said: 'Some of us say it is equal to one Hajj, and some of us say it is equal to one 'Umrah.' He said: 'It is equal to an accepted 'Umrah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah to the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this narration resolves a juristic debate by affirming that the spiritual reward of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s grave is equivalent to an accepted 'Umrah, emphasizing its status as a distinct act of devotion rather than merely a supplementary pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the unique ontological status of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology, where their graves serve as focal points for divine grace (barakah) comparable to the Kaaba. The designation of 'accepted' (maqbulah) implies that the visitor’s sincerity and adherence to ritual purity are essential for the reward to be fully realized.
